name: Palal
overview: Palal was a male figure noted for his role in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls following the exile. Specifically, he is recognized for repairing the wall of Jerusalem in front of the Angle, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:25. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Palal means 'he has judged,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a meaningful root. This name was not given directly by God but carries significance in its meaning within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Palal is identified as the son of Uzai, establishing a direct paternal relationship mentioned explicitly in Scripture (Nehemiah 3:25). Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Palal's significance lies in his contribution to the physical and spiritual restoration of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. By repairing the wall in front of the Angle, he played a vital role in reestablishing the city's defenses, which was crucial for the community's security and identity. His work exemplifies the collective effort of God's people to rebuild and renew their covenantal life.
